topics.name: Food webs & interdependence
topics.sci: Energy and matter flow between organisms; removing one species has flow-on effects through a network, not a single chain.

topics.name: Sampling a local ecosystem
topics.sci: Using quadrats/transects to estimate abundance; deciding sample size and placement to get representative, reliable data.

topics.name: Balanced vs unbalanced forces
topics.sci: Net force determines change in motion; a common misconception is that constant motion needs a constant force ('force implies moving').

topics.name: Interpreting a graph with an anomaly
topics.sci: Reading trends from a graph; deciding whether an off-trend point is a real signal or a measurement error before drawing a conclusion.

topics.name: Designing a first-hand investigation
topics.sci: Building a fair, valid, reliable method — e.g. testing which surface harbours more microbes — by isolating variables and controlling confounds.

topics.name: Evaluating evidence on a health claim
topics.sci: Weighing sample size, methodology, replication and conflict of interest; separating correlation from causation in a media health claim.

topics.name: Conservation of mass
topics.sci: Mass is conserved in a chemical reaction; a common misconception is that mass is 'lost' when gas is produced or a candle burns away.

topics.name: Punnett squares & inheritance
topics.sci: Predicting offspring ratios from genotypes; a common error is confusing genotype with phenotype and misreading probabilities as certainties.

topics.name: Extended response on immunity
topics.sci: Writing a mark-worthy extended response — e.g. explaining the immune response — structured to the marking criteria and the question's verb.

topics.name: Chemical equilibrium
topics.sci: Dynamic equilibrium and Le Châtelier's principle; the classic misconception is picturing equilibrium as a reaction that has stopped rather than running both ways at equal rates.

topics.name: Titration calculations
topics.sci: Multi-step quantitative problem-solving (moles, concentration, stoichiometry); errors often come from unmonitored unit-tracking and not sense-checking the final figure.

topics.name: Projectile motion
topics.sci: Independence of horizontal and vertical motion; students commonly (and wrongly) treat the two components as linked, or think a faster horizontal launch delays the fall.

areas.label: Investigating Science (2017)
areas.sub: Nature & practice of science · depth study

topics.name: Depth study across a term
topics.sci: A multi-week self-directed investigation: forming a question, planning, monitoring progress, and evaluating the whole process — the ideal home for sustained metacognition.
